title: Swiss phenology data replicate the German overprediction of frost by a 1 January heat-sum measure; the high-elevation frost increase of 1975-2016 did not continue in 2017-2025
abstract: Question: in Switzerland, does a climate-only frost measure that assumes a fixed heat sum from 1 January (Zohner et al. 2020) follow frost after observed spring onset, as tested for Germany in sci:6d514d9c, and did frost exposure after onset increase more at high elevation, as Vitasse et al. (2018) reported from modelled phenology for 1975-2016? Data: 39,400 MeteoSwiss observed onset records (leaf-out or needle emergence of 8 trees, flowering of cherry, apple, pear; 50% stage) at 146 stations (200-1,933 m, 1951-2025), each with daily minimum and mean temperature from the nearest SwissMetNet station (median 7.3 km, 35 m height difference). Exposure is a minimum at or below -2 C (also below 0 C, -4 C) after onset to 30 June. Pair fixed effects, two-way clustered errors by year and pair. Tests were fixed before the outcomes. Results: (1) Per extra 50 degree-days in January-February, the observed-minus-proxy exposure difference (below 0 C) was -9.6 pp (95% CI -11.5 to -7.7) for leaf-out and -5.2 pp (-6.7 to -3.7) for flowering (Germany: -10.4 and -7.3). It was below zero in all 27 subsets (taxa, regions, elevation groups, periods). A heat sum above 5 C from 1 March removed the leaf-out bias. (2) In 1975-2016, the -2 C exposure trend was 3.7 pp per decade larger at stations at or above 800 m (CI 1.1 to 6.4), because onset advanced faster there while the last frost advanced equally. This did not continue: in 2017-2025, high stations had 19.8% exposure against 25.2% predicted by the 1975-2016 model (CI of difference -14.6 to +4.8; at 0 C -17.4 pp, CI -29.1 to -4.9), and low stations had more frost than predicted (2017, 2021). Over 1959-2025 the contrast was +0.8 pp per decade (CI -1.2 to 2.9). In an exploratory window scan, no window ending in 2020-2025 had a contrast with a CI above zero. Limitations: screen temperature at nearby stations, no damage data, 50% stage, few records before 1975, few high stations, dependence on a few frost years; the 5 cm ground minimum did not show the 1975-2016 contrast.

citations.reason: We replicate its main test (fixed 1 January heat-sum proxy versus observed onset) with independent Swiss data and reuse its definitions.
Its result that the Swiss leaf-out elevation gradient stopped decreasing after 2016 agrees with the end of the high-elevation frost increase.
Related thermal-time analysis of leaf-out sensitivity with the same Swiss phenology data.
Related test of freezing exposure after cherry bloom at Liestal.
Vitasse et al. 2018: we test the high-elevation frost increase with observed dates and an out-of-sample period.
Zohner et al. 2020: we test the fixed heat-sum assumption of their climate-only frost measure.
